quiz.question: Why is traditional DevOps insufficient for managing machine learning systems?
options: DevOps cannot deploy applications to the cloud
ML application behavior depends on code, model weights, and changing data distributions, requiring dataset and model lifecycle versioning
DevOps only works with compiled C++ binaries
ML models cannot be packaged inside Docker containers
quiz.explanation: ML systems are uniquely stateful and data-driven; their performance can change without any code change when underlying data distributions shift.

quiz.question: Why should large foundation model weights be decoupled from Docker container images?
options: Docker does not support files larger than 100 megabytes
Baking multi-gigabyte weights into images causes massive CI/CD bloat, slow registry transfers, and prevents independent code updates
Model weights run faster when stored in Git repositories
Container runtimes cannot read binary weight files
quiz.explanation: Decoupling weights allows application containers to remain lightweight (<250MB), enabling rapid CI/CD cycles while mounting or streaming weights from object storage.

quiz.question: What is the primary advantage of a multi-stage Docker build for Python applications?
options: It allows the container to run on both Windows and Linux simultaneously
It separates build tools and compilers from the final runtime image, drastically reducing container size and security vulnerabilities
It automatically trains machine learning models during the build step
It eliminates the need for requirements.txt
quiz.explanation: Multi-stage builds discard build tools, compilers, and pip caches, producing slim production images with smaller attack surfaces and faster pull times.

quiz.question: How do modern MLflow Model Aliases (@champion / @challenger) improve model deployments?
options: They automatically delete older model versions from disk
They allow inference services to resolve active production models dynamically without requiring application redeployment or code changes
They convert PyTorch models into JavaScript code
They enforce password authentication on model weights
quiz.explanation: Aliases allow inference clients to query '@champion' while operators reassign the alias pointer upon successful model validation.

quiz.question: How does DVC track large datasets without committing binary files into Git?
options: It compresses datasets into zip files before committing them to Git
It computes SHA-256 hashes, stores raw files in remote storage (S3/GCS), and commits lightweight .dvc metadata pointer files to Git
It converts datasets into SQL tables inside PostgreSQL
It deletes old datasets whenever new files are added
quiz.explanation: DVC tracks data by storing raw files in content-addressable storage while committing tiny .dvc pointer files into Git.

quiz.question: What is the primary operational mechanism of a Canary deployment?
options: Instantly switching 100% of traffic from an old version to a new version
Routing a small percentage of live production traffic to the new model version while monitoring error rates and latency before expanding rollout
Running all requests in a development sandbox without user traffic
Rebuilding the model from scratch every time a user logs in
quiz.explanation: Canary rollouts expose a new version to a small slice of production traffic (e.g. 5%), mitigating the blast radius of unexpected regressions.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of a Kubernetes Readiness Probe for an LLM inference pod?
options: To restart the container if CPU usage exceeds 90%
To verify that model weights have finished loading into GPU memory before routing user traffic to the pod
To run automated unit tests on the container
To check whether the developer has logged into Docker Hub
quiz.explanation: Readiness probes prevent traffic from reaching slow-loading model pods until weights are allocated and endpoints are ready to serve inference.

quiz.question: What is Data Drift (Covariate Shift)?
options: A database disk corruption error
A shift in the statistical distribution of input features P(X) compared to the baseline training dataset
A bug where the model produces random outputs
An increase in API server memory consumption
quiz.explanation: Data drift occurs when incoming production prompt or feature distributions differ significantly from the data used during model training.

quiz.question: What is the difference between Data Drift and Concept Drift?
options: Data drift affects images; concept drift affects text
Data drift is a change in input distribution P(X); concept drift is a change in the relationship between inputs and target outputs P(Y|X)
They are identical terms with no practical difference
Concept drift only occurs during local development
quiz.explanation: Data drift represents shifting inputs; concept drift represents a fundamental change in the definition of the correct target output for given inputs.

quiz.question: In a statistical drift test like Kolmogorov-Smirnov, what indicates that drift has occurred?
options: A p-value greater than 0.99
A p-value less than the significance threshold (typically p < 0.05)
The test takes longer than 10 seconds to execute
The dataset contains duplicate rows
quiz.explanation: A p-value < 0.05 rejects the null hypothesis that reference and production datasets come from the same distribution, confirming drift.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of Shadow Deployment in Generative AI systems?
options: Hiding model weights behind encryption keys
Duplicating production user prompts to a candidate model in the background to evaluate real-world quality without exposing users to risk
Running models only during off-peak nighttime hours
Training models without supervised human labels
quiz.explanation: Shadow deployments mirror live traffic to candidate models, allowing safe benchmarking of latency and output quality without affecting users.

quiz.question: What are the two core telemetry metrics used to evaluate LLM generation responsiveness?
options: Disk I/O and RAM usage
Time to First Token (TTFT) and Time Per Output Token (TPOT)
Ethernet bandwidth and CPU fan speed
SQL query time and table row count
quiz.explanation: TTFT measures prefill responsiveness; TPOT measures the throughput of incremental autoregressive decode iterations.
